title: Decide with Confidence
subtitle: Make better decisions  faster, with less regret.
description: Most business failures are not failures of effort they are failures of decision. The wrong market entered. The wrong hire kept too long. The wrong pivot made too late. This module gives you ten frameworks for structured decision-making from rapid frameworks for daily decisions to deep analytical tools for irreversible ones. Combined with AI, these frameworks turn gut-feel decisions into evidence-based ones without slowing you down.

internal.bestWhen: Before any irreversible or high-stakes decision

internal.priorities: What could go seriously wrong — and how bad is it?
internal.bestWhen: Mapping the tail risks before committing

internal.priorities: Is this decision consistent with where we said we are going?
internal.bestWhen: When a decision feels right but contradicts the strategy

internal.priorities: Can we actually execute this — with the people and budget we have?
internal.bestWhen: Before committing to any plan that requires operational delivery

internal.priorities: Which cognitive biases are distorting this right now?
internal.bestWhen: When you notice the team is unusually aligned — suspiciously fast

internal.priorities: What does the evidence actually say versus what we believe?
internal.bestWhen: When a decision is being made on instinct that should be made on data

outside.priorities: Find every weakness in the plan before an adversary does
outside.bestWhen: Before launching, announcing, or committing publicly

outside.priorities: What happens when this goes wrong? Are you ready?
outside.bestWhen: For any decision that would be hard to reverse

outside.priorities: Argues the opposite position as hard as possible
outside.bestWhen: When the room agrees too quickly

outside.priorities: Looking back — what would you wish you had decided?
outside.bestWhen: For life-scale decisions where short- term and long-term diverge

roleProfile.question: Who should stress-test your most important decisions?
roleProfile.lead: Most bad decisions were not obviously bad at the time — they had a good first-order case and a hidden second-order cost. The roles on this page are designed to surface what you cannot see from inside your own reasoning. Some will challenge your logic. Some will challenge your assumptions. One will challenge whether you are even asking the right question.
roleProfile.sharpen: HOW TO MAKE ANY ROLE SHARPER 1. Add years of experience: "...with 15 years in enterprise SaaS" produces different depth than just the title. 2. Add what they care most about: "You care most about [X]" shapes every word of the output. 3. Add their communication style: "Be direct. Flag risks first.
